title: CALVING AND CALF MANAGEMENT
text:
CALVING AND CALF MANAGEMENT

Objectives:
1. To learn the calving process.
2. To familiarize the common problems in calving.
3. To know how to manage the neonates and calves.

Definition of terms:
Neonate - new born animal.
Lactation - the process of making milk.
Lactation period - is the length of milk production period after calving. Standard is 305 days.
Gestation - the period of time between conception and birth. Standard is 285 days.
Parturition - act of giving birth.
Dystocia - is the abnormal or difficulty in parturition.
Colostrum - first milk of the cow, rich in antibodies, nutrients and minerals.

Pre-calving management:
1. Separate the cow due for calving.
a) Vitamin administration
b) Perform rectal palpation to determine the presentation and size of the fetus.
c) Check the cow's udder for early signs of mastitis.
2. Place the cow in a clean and dry calving area days before its expected calving date.
a) Calving pens should be properly cleaned and disinfected before restocking.
b) Provide clean and dry beddings especially in calving pens with concrete flooring.
c) Calving pens should be spacious for free movement and allow proper ventilation.

Stages of parturition:
Stage 1: Calf moves into position as the cervix and birth canal begin to dilate.
Signs:
- Vocalization and restless behavior
- Raised tail head
- Increased urination and defecation
- Full udder

facts: The learning objectives of Calving and Calf Management are: to learn the calving process, to familiarize common problems in calving, and to know how to manage neonates and calves.
A neonate is defined as a newborn animal.
Lactation is defined as the process of making milk.
The lactation period is the length of milk production period after calving, with a standard duration of 305 days.
Gestation is the period of time between conception and birth, with a standard duration of 285 days.
Parturition is the act of giving birth.
Dystocia refers to abnormal or difficult parturition.
Colostrum is the first milk produced by the cow, rich in antibodies, nutrients, and minerals.

Pre-calving management includes separating the cow due for calving, administering vitamins, performing rectal palpation to determine fetal presentation and size, and checking the udder for early signs of mastitis.
The cow should be placed in a clean and dry calving area days before its expected calving date.

Calving pens must be properly cleaned and disinfected before restocking, provided with clean and dry beddings (especially on concrete flooring), and must be spacious for free movement and allow proper ventilation.
Stage 1 of parturition occurs when the calf moves into position as the cervix and birth canal begin to dilate.
Signs of Stage 1 parturition include vocalization and restless behavior, a raised tail head, increased urination and defecation, and a full udder.

questions.question: Why is rectal palpation performed as part of pre-calving management?

options.B: To determine the presentation and size of the fetus
options.C: To test the cow for subclinical mastitis
options.D: To induce cervical dilation prior to delivery

questions.question: Which physiological event defines Stage 1 of parturition?

options.A: Complete expulsion of the calf through the birth canal
options.B: Expulsion of the placenta and fetal membranes
options.C: The calf moves into position as the cervix and birth canal begin to dilate
options.D: Immediate release of colostrum upon suckling

questions.question: Regarding pen preparation, clean and dry bedding is particularly emphasized for calving pens with which type of flooring?

options.A: True, it is especially emphasized for pens with concrete flooring
options.B: False, bedding is prohibited on concrete floors to prevent slipping
options.C: False, bedding is only required on packed dirt surfaces
options.D: False, bedding is replaced with rubber slats exclusively
